user.t:
You are hive agent "mesh-coder" (a ruflo coder). Read, in this order:
1. C:[REDACTED:high_entropy].md (the hive rules; APx has no license, so do not copy it).
2. BUS.md, cartographer.md, scout-synaptic.md, scout-latent.md and router-eval-REPORT.md in the same folder.
Target: C:/Users/mariu/neural-mesh (Rust).
Toolchain: use ~/.cargo/bin/cargo.exe with WinLibs mingw on PATH, because the `cargo` on PATH is an npm shim.

Implement the four top-ranked router upgrades, each opt-in and gated:
(1) Failure-class-aware feedback. Add a `--failure-class skill|spec|env` option to the CLI `feedback` command (and to the library).
- env failures (rate-limit, turn-limit, worktree block) do not touch skill weights or health benching. They update a separate per-agent dispatch-risk score, which `route` returns.
- Expose `feedback_opt(update_leader=false)` through this option.
(2) Label feedback mode. Add `feedback --label <agent>` for when the correct agent is known even if it wasn't the one picked. It is a supervised update.
(3) Embedding features for unseen wording. Use the existing Rust MiniLM encoder (encoder.rs) with CaseRouter or KnnRouter (with the 0.4 similarity floor) so that differently worded tasks share learning. Make it a selectable leader mode.
(4) Gate gaps:
- Add a 61-90 confirm split to src/bin/experiment.rs.
- Add a simulator scenario with ~18% skill-independent environment failures (for item 1).
- Add a Guarded row if it is cheap.
For each item, write a hypothesis first. Then evaluate it as the hive rules require:
- tune on 1-30 (or 1-8 where the harness does that), held-out 31-60, confirm 61-90;
- apply Holm across the tests;
- check no-regress elsewhere.
Also evaluate items 2 and 3 on the real 69-row replay. Its dataset and scripts are at C:[REDACTED:high_entropy] (dataset.jsonl, route-replay.mjs). Use leave-wording-out folds for item 3, against Hebbian label-fed's ~.68.
Keep defaults unchanged unless the gate is met. Commit the winners to neural-mesh's current branch, by explicit path, local only. Revert losers and record them in RD-LOG.md as honest negatives, in its existing round format (continue the numbering).
Other agents also edit neural-mesh: "ingestor" works only in ingest/, and "llm-smith" works in llm/ and may touch src/ for a front-end hook.
- Post on BUS.md which src files you are changing, before you start.
- Read BUS.md before each commit.
- Never revert or reformat another agent's changes.
- `cargo test --release --lib` must stay green (403+).
Return a concise report (≤ 30 lines): per item, the hypothesis, the numbers (n, seeds, CI, Holm), the verdict, and the commit hash or the reason for reverting.

handback.t:
mesh-coder report (neural-mesh, local commits on master, not pushed). lib tests 408 green (was 403), bin tests 22 green. Commits: 1e2ca01 (src/mesh.rs, src/bin/experiment.rs, results/r117_* logs, archived negatives) and ad48555 (src/main.rs, src/serve.rs, RD-LOG.md R117-R121).

Gate: experiment.rs tune seeds 1-8, held-out 31-60, confirm 61-90 (new `--held`), n=30 paired seeds x 2000 tasks, Holm over 16 tests per split. The committed 31-60 numbers in results/results.json reproduce bit-identically.

1. Failure class (`feedback --failure-class skill|spec|env`) - KEPT, opt-in.
 - Hypothesis: env failures (rate limit, turn limit, worktree block) must not train skill weights or health. Env goes to a per-agent dispatch-risk EMA instead, which `route` returns once any env failure has been recorded. `spec` = `feedback_opt(update_leader=false)`.
 - New sim scenario `env18`: random world plus 18% skill-independent env failures, heterogeneous per agent.
 - Shield minus unshielded mesh-robust: 31-60 +.0214 [+.0123,+.0305], 25 wins/3 losses, p_holm .0003. 61-90 +.0258 [+.0151,+.0364], 27/3, p_holm .0002.
 - No-regress: in the 6 original scenarios the shield equals mesh-robust bit for bit.
 - Env/spec feedback is not written to the --store journal (replay would feed it to the skill weights).
 - Limit: it stops the damage but does not route away from risky agents.

2. `feedback --label <agent> [--agent routed]` - no accuracy win; KEPT as opt-in convenience.
 - Real 69-row replay, prequential, 30 seeds: reward-only .338, existing two-call label workaround .658, `--label` .658. Paired over rows: +.000 [+.000,+.000], identical predictions, p_holm 1.0.
 - So the +.32 gain over reward-only already exists with two calls. `--label` saves one call, doesn't hit the wrong pick's health, and writes label=1 / wrong=0 lines to the journal.
 - Own code path (`cmd_feedback_label`), removable on its own if you read "no win" as "revert". Say so and I'll pull it.

3. Embedding features for unseen wording (MiniLM kNN prior, KnnRouter with smin .4 floor, CaseRouter) - REJECTED, code reverted, archived in results/r117_negatives/*.txt.
 - Leave-wording-out on the real replay: 46 folds, grouped by the first two alphabetic tokens of each prompt. Hebbian label-fed .627.
 - knn+hebbian .449 (-.178 [-.274,-.082], p_holm .0045); knn raw .420 (-.207, p_holm .0025); CaseRouter .391 (-.236 [-.347,-.124], p_holm .0009).
 - Post-hoc first-6-words variant: .507 / .493, n.s. Prequential knn+hebbian .579 vs .658, n.s.
 - Why: MiniLM neighbours share topic, not the phase verb that decides the agent. "Plan web app steps 1+2" and "Build web app steps 1+2" embed almost identically. The phase-verb rule (.913) was written after reading the data.
 - Not tried: verb-only text, learned projection. The sim has no text, so it cannot test this.

4. Gate gaps - KEPT (harness only).
 - Done: `--held 61-90` confirm split, `env18` scenario, and a Guarded row (`recommended_router`).
 - Guarded vs keyword in no-traps (where every learner was Holm-worse by .03-.04): +.0016 [-.0016,+.0048] on 31-60 and +.0043 [+.0010,+.0075] on 61-90, both inside ±.01 and not Holm-significant.
 - Guarded vs mesh-robust: Holm-beats it in fixed, no-traps, delay25 (31-60) and env18 (31-60), and is n.s. elsewhere. Never Holm-worse.
 - Not made the CLI default.

5. Discounted-UCB leader (queen note) - REJECTED, code reverted, archived.
 - Tuned on seeds 1-8 like every learner (gamma .923, alpha .1). Versus mesh-robust: 0 Holm wins and 0 Holm losses across 7 scenarios on both splits, raw differences -.010 to +.011. The 61-90 `random` gap of -.0077 has a raw CI just under 0 but did not survive Holm.
 - It beats the best baseline in 4-5 of 7 scenarios but is Holm-worse than keyword in no-traps (-.029 / -.026).
 - Replay: prequential +.028 n.s.; leave-wording-out +.040, p_holm .14.

Caveats: the 69-row replay is one project and one leader's labels; the sim failures and wordings are synthetic.
